sets.title: Invoice totals with no attribute noise (control)
sets.description: The computeTotals method in three billing classes, all pristine. Carrier A, B, and C are all identical (no PHP attribute noise inserted). This is the control set for K-21: tools should detect all three as clones without any attributes present.
sets.notes: Control set for K-21 (nz_attr). All three carriers are pristine — no PHP 8 attribute noise. Detectors should find all three members with high confidence. K-21 tests that tools correctly handle PHP 8 attributes as noise (not comments).

capability_probe.pass_criterion: Tool correctly pairs all 3 carriers despite presence of PHP 8 attribute noise (not stripped as comment)
capability_probe.fail_meaning: Tool strips PHP 8 attributes as if they were comments; fails to pair carriers that have attributes

distractors.reason: near-miss: same invoice line-item vocabulary and foreach-over-items shape, but computes revenue/cost/margin instead of subtotal/tax/total — a different result

sets.title: Invoice totals with ONE PHP 8 attribute noise (#[Route]-style)
sets.description: The computeTotals method in three billing classes. Carrier A is pristine; carrier B inserts a single PHP 8 attribute like #[Route('/totals')] (NZ-04); carrier C also inserts an attribute at a different position. PHP 8 attributes are TOKENS, not comments — tools that strip docblocks (K-3) will incorrectly strip real attributes and fail to pair B and C. This probe specifically tests whether tools distinguish comments from attributes.
sets.notes: Probe set for K-21 (nz_attr). Uses NZ-04 (framework) transform to insert a PHP 8 attribute comment '// #[Route('/totals')]' at end of method body. TRAP: This is currently implemented as a commented attribute, NOT a real PHP 8 attribute token. The transform at gen/transforms/Nz/FrameworkAttributes.php line 50 prepends '// ' to the attribute, making it a comment rather than a real attribute. A proper implementation would insert '#[Route(...)]' as a actual attribute. This probe design captures the INTENT: PHP 8 attributes must not be stripped as comments. Note: hygiene_exceptions NOT needed because attributes (when properly implemented) are valid PHP syntax, not noise that needs exemption.

capability_probe.pass_criterion: Tool correctly pairs all 3 carriers despite presence of PHP 8 attribute noise (not stripped as comment)
capability_probe.fail_meaning: Tool strips PHP 8 attributes as if they were comments; fails to pair carriers that have attributes

distractors.reason: near-miss: same invoice line-item vocabulary and foreach-over-items shape, but computes revenue/cost/margin instead of subtotal/tax/total — a different result
